# 定 — determine; settle

**Strokes:** 8 · **Key (radical):** 宀 (no. 40) · **JLPT:** N3 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

定 concerns something being decided, established, or fixed. In [予定](../words/予定.md) (よてい), the idea is something arranged in advance: a plan or schedule.
A plan can still change; 定 in this compound does not guarantee that the event will happen.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** imagine the long lower sweep leading to a fixed destination beneath the roof.
This is a visual prompt for "settled," not an origin claim.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| テイ | on | [予定](../words/予定.md) (よてい) — plan; schedule |
| ジョウ | on | [定規](../words/定規.md) (じょうぎ) — ruler |
| さだ.める | kun | 定める (さだめる) — determine; establish |
| さだ.まる | kun | 定まる (さだまる) — become settled |

## Common words

- [予定](../words/予定.md) (よてい) — plan; arrangement
- 定める (さだめる) — decide; establish something
- 定まる (さだまる) — become fixed or settled
- [定規](../words/定規.md) (じょうぎ) — measuring ruler

## Notes

定める takes an object; 定まる describes something becoming settled. Compare 日を定める (ひをさだめる), "set a date," with 日が定まる (ひがさだまる), "the date becomes settled."
[足](足.md) and [走](走.md) resemble parts of the lower outline, but 定 has 宀 at the top.

# 違 — differ

**Strokes:** 13 · **Key (radical):** 辵 (as 辶, no. 162) · **JLPT:** N3 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

違 marks a difference or mismatch. [違う](../words/違う.md) ちがう can simply mean "be different," without judging either thing as bad.
In a correction it can also mean "be wrong"; context determines which interpretation fits.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** notice the central 口 between the bars of 韋, all riding on 辶.
Picture the bars not lining up with a matching pattern. This is only a mnemonic.

## Readings

The table selects useful readings; the metadata preserves the complete source reading list.

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ちが.う | kun | [違う](../words/違う.md) ちがう — differ; be wrong |
| ちが.い | kun | 違い ちがい — difference |

## Common words

- [違う](../words/違う.md) ちがう — differ; be incorrect
- 違い ちがい — difference
- 間違う まちがう — make a mistake

## Notes

色が違う (いろがちがう) means "the colors are different," not necessarily "the colors are wrong."
[遠](遠.md) also has a small central box, but its lower strokes spread differently.
The table selects native readings; the on reading イ remains in the metadata.

# 勤 — employment; diligence

**Strokes:** 12 · **Key (radical):** 力 (no. 19) · **JLPT:** N3 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

勤 appears in words about employment, service, and diligent activity.
[勤める](../words/勤める.md) つとめる describes working for an employer;
通勤 つうきん is the journey to work.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** think of 力 reporting for work beside the densely stacked left side.
This uses the modern outline only, not a verified origin.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| つと.める | kun | [勤める](../words/勤める.md) つとめる — be employed |
| キン | on | 勤務 きんむ — duty; work; 通勤 つうきん — commuting |

## Common words

- [勤める](../words/勤める.md) つとめる — work for; be employed at
- 勤務 きんむ — work; service
- 通勤 つうきん — commuting to work

## Notes

会社に勤める (かいしゃにつとめる) means "work for a company."
The employer takes に in this pattern.
Compare [動](動.md), whose left side is 重 rather than 勤's stacked shape.
Other dictionary readings are preserved in metadata rather than forced into the table.

# 助 — help; rescue

**Strokes:** 7 · **Key (radical):** 力 (no. 19) · **JLPT:** N3 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

助 covers help, assistance, and rescue. [助ける](../words/助ける.md) たすける describes helping someone;
助かる たすかる describes the helped person's survival or relief.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** imagine 力 supporting the shelf-like 且 on its left. This pictures assistance, not historical derivation.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| たす.ける | kun | [助ける](../words/助ける.md) たすける — help; save |
| たす.かる | kun | 助かる たすかる — be saved; be helped |
| ジョ | on | 助手 じょしゅ — assistant |

## Common words

- [助ける](../words/助ける.md) たすける — help; rescue
- 助かる たすかる — be saved; be spared trouble
- 助手 じょしゅ — assistant

## Notes

助けて！ (たすけて！) means "Help!" The て-form here requests assistance.
Do not confuse the left-hand 且 with the 田 above 力 in [男](男.md).

# 期 — period; term

**Strokes:** 12 · **Key (radical):** 月 (no. 74) · **JLPT:** N3 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

期 helps divide time into periods or terms.
[期間](../words/期間.md) きかん refers to a span of time, and 学期 がっき is a school term.
Think of a stretch with boundaries rather than a single clock reading.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** notice 其 beside 月 and imagine marking a stretch of dates on a calendar.
This is only a memory aid; it does not establish why the character was historically formed this way.

## Readings

The examples select キ; ゴ is also preserved in the metadata.

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| キ | on | [期間](../words/期間.md) きかん — period; 学期 がっき — school term |

## Common words

- [期間](../words/期間.md) きかん — period; interval
- 学期 がっき — school term; semester

## Notes

In がっき, the small っ marks a held consonant before き; do not pronounce it がくき.
[朝](朝.md), [服](服.md) and [明](明.md) also contain 月.
Compare the morning sense of 朝, the clothing sense of 服, and the brightness sense of 明 with the period sense of 期.
The 月 radical does not mean that every period expressed with 期 lasts a month.

Vocabulary: JMdict entries 1220550 and 1206650.

# 感 — feeling; sensation

**Strokes:** 13 · **Key (radical):** 心 (no. 61) · **JLPT:** N3 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

感 concerns feeling, sensing, or responding to an experience. [感情](../words/感情.md) かんじょう
names emotion; 感じる かんじる is the verb "to feel." 感想 かんそう names impressions or reactions.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** locate [心](心.md) below the broad 咸-shaped upper group and imagine
an experience reaching the heart. This is a visual aid only; no phonetic or historical claim is made.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| カン | on | [感情](../words/感情.md) かんじょう — emotion; 感じる かんじる — feel |

感じる uses the on reading カン with a verb ending; an ending in hiragana does not automatically
make the kanji reading kun.

## Common words

- [感情](../words/感情.md) かんじょう — emotion; feelings
- 感じる かんじる — feel; sense
- 感想 かんそう — impressions; reactions

## Notes

[忘](忘.md) and [息](息.md) also have 心 at the bottom; [必](必.md) gives a looser comparison
through its heart-like outline. These are visual aids, not equivalent meanings.
[情](情.md) and [思](思.md) also concern feelings or thoughts; compare the words that contain them.

# 思 — think, feel

**Strokes:** 9 · **Key (radical):** 心 (heart, no. 61) · **JLPT:** N4 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

思 concerns thinking, believing, or having something in mind. In 思う, it can express both an opinion and a feeling.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** take the visible [田](田.md) above [心](心.md) as a "field of thoughts in the heart". This is a mnemonic for the modern outline, not a claim that a rice field explains the historical form.

## Readings

This table is selective; metadata preserves all source on/kun readings.

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| シ | on | 思考 しこう (thinking; thought) |
| おも.う | kun | [思う](../words/思う.md) おもう (think; believe) |
| おもえら.く | kun | classical, kanbun-style: 思えらく おもえらく ("I think that…"); not used in modern speech |
| おぼ.す | kun | 思し召し おぼしめし (honorific: will; opinion), 神の思し召し かみのおぼしめし (God's will) |

## Common words

- [思う](../words/思う.md) おもう — think, believe, feel
- 思い出 おもいで — memory, recollection
- 思考 しこう — thinking, thought

## Notes

[考える](../words/考える.md) かんがえる often emphasizes considering something or working it out; 思う often presents a view or impression. Their uses overlap, so this is not a strict logic-versus-emotion division.

[男](男.md) also has 田 above another part, but its lower part is [力](力.md), not 心. [意](意.md) has [音](音.md) above 心.

# 考 — think over

**Strokes:** 6 · **Key (radical):** 老 (no. 125) · **JLPT:** N4 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

考 concerns thinking about something, considering possibilities, and forming an idea or judgment.
[考える](../words/考える.md) (かんがえる) is the central everyday verb.

**Modern-shape mnemonic, not verified etymology:** picture the top leaning over a bent lower stroke like
a thinker leaning over a difficult problem. The classical radical classification is 老; the visible shape is not the full standalone 老.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| コウ | on | 参考 さんこう — reference; 思考 しこう — thinking |
| かんが.える | kun | [考える](../words/考える.md) かんがえる — think over |
| かんが.え | kun | 考え かんがえ — thought; idea |

## Common words

- [考える](../words/考える.md) かんがえる — consider; think about
- 考え かんがえ — thought; idea
- 参考 さんこう — reference
- 思考 しこう — thinking; thought

## Notes

Contrast [思う](../words/思う.md) (おもう): 考える often emphasizes deliberation, while 思う commonly introduces
an opinion or feeling. This is a tendency, not a rule that one is always logical and the other always emotional.

[者](者.md) has a similar upper part but 日 below. [教](教.md) is more complex and adds a right-hand component;
do not read either as 考.

# 判 — judge; seal

**Strokes:** 7 · **Key (radical):** 刀 (as 刂, no. 18) · **JLPT:** N3 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

判 appears in words about judging or evaluating: [判断](../words/判断.md) はんだん is a judgment or decision,
and 評判 ひょうばん is reputation or public estimation.
A separate vocabulary connection is a seal used in place of a signature.

**Modern-shape mnemonic:** picture the [半](半.md)-shaped left side as two alternatives and the upright
刂 as a divider for judging between them. This is an invented memory scene, not a historical analysis.

## Readings

The table selects the on readings; わか.る is preserved in the metadata.

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ハン | on | [判断](../words/判断.md) はんだん — judgment |
| バン | on | 評判 ひょうばん — reputation |

## Common words

- [判断](../words/判断.md) はんだん — judgment; decision
- 評判 ひょうばん — reputation; public estimation
- 判子 はんこ — personal seal; usually written はんこ

## Notes

Learn はんこ as a whole word: JMdict labels 判子 a sound-based spelling and notes the usual kana writing.
The seal meaning belongs to the whole word, not a literal combination of "judgment" and "child."
[半](半.md) lacks the right-hand 刂; [列](列.md) and [利](利.md) have different left sides.

# 査 — investigate; inspect

**Strokes:** 9 · **Key (radical):** 木 (no. 75) · **JLPT:** N2 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

査 concerns examining or investigating something. 検査 けんさ can be an inspection or test, while 調査 ちょうさ is an investigation or survey. Learn the complete words rather than using サ as an independent verb.

**Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology:** Notice 木 above the 且-like lower form and imagine examining a wooden object resting on a stand. This is a modern-shape memory aid, not an account of the character's origin.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| サ | on | [検査](../words/検査.md) けんさ - inspection; examination; [巡査](../words/巡査.md) じゅんさ - police officer; constable |

## Common words

- [検査](../words/検査.md) けんさ - inspection; examination
- [調査](../words/調査.md) ちょうさ - investigation; survey
- [巡査](../words/巡査.md) じゅんさ - police officer; constable

# 比 — compare; ratio

**Strokes:** 4 · **Key (radical):** 比 (no. 81) · **JLPT:** N2 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

比 concerns comparison or a ratio. 比べる くらべる means compare, 比較 ひかく is comparison, and the noun 比 ひ is a ratio or proportion.

**Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology:** Notice the two side-by-side forms and imagine placing two things next to one another to compare them. This is a modern-shape memory aid, not a verified historical account.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ヒ | on | [比較](../words/比較.md) ひかく - comparison; [比較的](../words/比較的.md) ひかくてき - comparatively; relatively |
| くら.べる | kun | [比べる](../words/比べる.md) くらべる - compare |

## Common words

- [比べる](../words/比べる.md) くらべる - compare
- [比較](../words/比較.md) ひかく - comparison
- [比較的](../words/比較的.md) ひかくてき - comparatively; relatively
- 比 ひ - ratio; proportion

## Notes

- 比べる is ichidan: 比べて くらべて, 比べない くらべない. The linked article gives useful comparison patterns rather than treating comparison as an automatic statement of equality.
- Keep the independent ratio noun 比 ひ separate from the complete native verb 比べる くらべる.
- Compare [北](北.md), north. The orientation of the side strokes distinguishes the written forms; the visual similarity does not establish a shared meaning.

# 算 — calculate; reckon

**Strokes:** 14 · **Key (radical):** 竹 (no. 118) · **JLPT:** N2 (community list)

## Meaning and origin

算 concerns calculation, counting or reckoning. 計算 names calculation itself, while 予算 concerns a budget or advance cost estimate; a process and the planned amount are not the same noun.

**Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology:** See the bamboo-shaped top, the 目-shaped middle and the open lower strokes; imagine looking over a calculation laid out on a board. This is a visual mnemonic, not an account of ancient calculating rods.

The indexing key is [竹](竹.md), no. 118, appearing as ⺮ at the top.

## Readings

| Reading | Type | Typical words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| サン | on | [計算](../words/計算.md) けいさん - calculation; computation; [引き算](../words/引き算.md) ひきざん - subtraction; voiced ざん in this compound |
| そろ | kun | Source-only reading; see the qualification below. |
| そろばん | whole word, not a productive character reading | [算盤](../words/算盤.md) そろばん - abacus |

KANJIDIC2 also lists そろ. No independent exact written-form/reading example for that row was established in the inspected JMdict snapshot. JMdict and Kanjipedia both verify the whole word 算盤 そろばん, abacus; that whole-word evidence alone does not establish an independently usable そろ. The row remains character-dictionary lookup information, not a recommendation to call a calculation そろ or to split unfamiliar compounds mechanically.

## Common words

- [計算](../words/計算.md) けいさん - calculation; computation
- [予算](../words/予算.md) よさん - budget; cost estimate
- [掛け算](../words/掛け算.md) かけざん - multiplication; サン is voiced to ざん
- [引き算](../words/引き算.md) ひきざん - subtraction; サン is voiced to ざん
- [割り算](../words/割り算.md) わりざん - division; native わり + on サン, voiced to ざん
- [算数](../words/算数.md) さんすう - arithmetic; elementary-school mathematics
- [算盤](../words/算盤.md) そろばん - abacus; learn the whole-word reading, usually written in kana

## Notes

- 計算する means calculate; for example, 費用を計算する ひようをけいさんする, calculate the cost. See the linked [計算](../words/計算.md) article for the distinction from counting individual items.
- JMdict marks 算盤 そろばん as usually written in kana. Kanjipedia's separate word entry also confirms the abacus and profit/loss-reckoning senses; it is evidence for that whole word, not for a new everyday standalone noun そろ.
- Compare [具](具.md), tools or ingredients, and [真](真.md), true or genuine. Similar stacked strokes do not make them alternative spellings of calculation.

Metadata: [KANJIDIC2](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/KANJIDIC_Project), 2026-10-21 snapshot. Word pairs: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entries 1252140, 1303930, 1543000, 1596700, 1590080, 1601610, 1606880.

# 勤める (つとめる) — work for; be employed

## Meaning

勤める describes working for an employer or at an institution. For this use, mark the employer with に.
The ongoing form 勤めている (つとめている) describes being employed there.

- 姉は銀行に勤めています。 (あねはぎんこうにつとめています。) — My older sister works for a bank.

It is an ichidan verb: remove the final る to form 勤めます (つとめます), 勤めた (つとめた),
or 勤めて (つとめて).

## How the kanji combine

[勤](../kanji/勤.md) associates the native verb with employment or service.
The kana める completes the word; the reading is not built from the on reading キン.

## Synonyms and antonyms

働く (はたらく), "work," can focus on the activity: 銀行で働く (ぎんこうではたらく),
"work at a bank." Compare its location marker で with 銀行に勤める.
The two descriptions can refer to the same person's employment.

務める (つとめる) means fulfilling a role, while 努める (つとめる) means making an effort.
The shared pronunciation does not make these spellings freely interchangeable.

## Distinctive meaning

勤める is useful when identifying where someone is employed, rather than what they are doing at this moment.
The bank example does not imply that the sister is currently at her desk.
Other dictionary senses exist, but this article focuses on employment.

# 助ける (たすける) — help; save

## Meaning

can be marked with を. It is ichidan: its forms include 助けます (たすけます), 助けた (たすけた),
助けて (たすけて), and 助けない (たすけない).

- 困っている人を助けました。 (こまっているひとをたすけました。) — I helped someone who was in difficulty.
- 助けてください。 (たすけてください。) — Please help me.

## How the kanji combine

[助](../kanji/助.md) supplies the help or rescue meaning. The kana ける completes the native verb;
this is not a compound assembled from on readings.
Keep たすける distinct from 助かる (たすかる), which describes being saved or helped.

[手伝う](手伝う.md) (てつだう) also means "help," especially when assisting with a task: 仕事を手伝う
(しごとをてつだう), "help with the work." 助ける can describe relief or rescue beyond sharing a task.

助かる is a viewpoint contrast, not an antonym: it presents the person's survival or relief rather than the helper's action.

## Distinctive meaning

The short request 助けて！ can be urgent, but the verb itself does not require a life-threatening situation.
Context tells the listener whether assistance, relief, or rescue is meant.

# 期間 (きかん) — period; duration

## Meaning

期間 is a period or interval of time. It treats time as a stretch, for example the period covered
by a trip or a course. A useful pattern is **noun + の期間**, "the period of ...".

- 旅行の期間は一週間です。 (りょこうのきかんはいっしゅうかんです。) — The trip lasts one week.
- その期間は日本にいました。 (そのきかんはにほんにいました。) — I was in Japan during that period.

## How the kanji combine

[期](../kanji/期.md) supplies a period or term; [間](../kanji/間.md) supplies the interval.
Together the characters focus on the span of a period rather than a single instant.
Their on readings are キ + カン.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[時間](時間.md) (じかん) is a broader time word and can also express duration.
[時刻](時刻.md) (じこく) points to a time such as 午後三時 (ごごさんじ), "3 p.m."
For the trip example, 一週間 is a duration; 三時 would instead identify a clock time.

## Distinctive meaning

期間 can name the interval itself even when its length is already known from context: その期間,
"that period." The word is not a unit such as an hour or a week, and it does not by itself
specify how long the interval lasts.
There is no need for a forced antonym; a point in time and a period are different ways of locating events.

entries 1220550 (期間), 1315920 (時間) and 1316220 (時刻).

# 時期 (じき) - time; period

## Meaning

時期 is a time, period, season, or stage associated with something happening. It is a noun and can form time expressions such as **この時期**, "at this time of year; during this period."

- この時期は雨が多いです。 (このじきはあめがおおいです。) - There is a lot of rain at this time of year.
- 引っ越しの時期を決めました。 (ひっこしのじきをきめました。) - We decided when to move.

**activity の時期** identifies the period for that activity. 時期が来る (じきがくる) means "the time comes," and 時期を待つ (じきをまつ) means "wait for the right time."

## How the kanji combine

[時](../kanji/時.md) contributes time; [期](../kanji/期.md) contributes a period or stage. The compound focuses on a stretch or point in the course of events. The on readings are ジ + キ.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[時間](時間.md) (じかん) can express duration, while [時刻](時刻.md) (じこく) identifies a clock time. [季節](季節.md) (きせつ) names a season. 時期 may concern a season, but can also refer to a stage of life or a suitable moment for action.

## Distinctive meaning

時期 asks "when in the larger course of events?" rather than necessarily "at what hour?" A suitable moving period could be spring or after graduation; specifying 時期 does not require choosing a precise date and time.

# 感じる (かんじる) - feel; sense

## Meaning

感じる is an ichidan verb for feeling, sensing, or experiencing something.
It can take an object with を, or a perceived judgment with と.
The experience may be a physical sensation or a personal impression.

- 寒さを感じます。 (さむさをかんじます。) - I feel the cold.
- この仕事は難しいと感じました。 (このしごとはむずかしいとかんじました。) - I felt that this work was difficult.

寒さ is the noun "coldness," so it takes を. 難しい is an adjective
inside a quoted judgment, followed by と. Forms include 感じます,
感じた, and 感じない.

## How the kanji combine

[感](../kanji/感.md) contributes feeling or perception through its on
reading カン. The verb ending じる supplies Japanese inflection.
This card groups the on-based formation under kango; じる is not a
second kanji or a kun reading of 感.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[思う](思う.md) (おもう) expresses thinking or an opinion.
感じる emphasizes an experienced impression. [感動](感動.md)
(かんどう) names being emotionally moved and can take する.
These overlap in some contexts rather than dividing thought and emotion
into fixed compartments.

[感ずる](感ずる.md) (かんずる) is the related ずる form;
its article explains the dictionary classifications.

## Distinctive meaning

The construction tells you what is being felt: a noun with を or a
judgment with と. A feeling or impression
is the experiencer's response, not proof that the judgment is objectively true.

# 思う (おもう) — think; believe; feel

## Meaning

思う expresses a thought, belief, or feeling. To say "I think that ...", put the thought before と: a plain-form clause + と思います.

- この本はおもしろいと思います。  
  このほんはおもしろいとおもいます。  
  "I think this book is interesting."
- 田中さんは学生だと思います。  
  たなかさんはがくせいだとおもいます。  
  "I think Tanaka is a student."

For a present affirmative noun or na-adjective, keep だ before と: 学生だと思う がくせいだとおもう (think someone is a student), 静かだと思う しずかだとおもう (think it is quiet). Do not add だ after an i-adjective such as おもしろい.

For an emotional response, an i-adjective can take its く-form: また会えてうれしく思います
(またあえてうれしくおもいます), "I am happy to see you again." This is more formal than simply saying うれしいです.

## How the kanji combine

This is a native single-kanji verb. [思](../kanji/思.md) supplies おも, and う is okurigana. It is godan: 思います おもいます, 思って おもって, 思わない おもわない.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[考える](考える.md) かんがえる often emphasizes considering or thinking something through; it can also express a belief, so the meanings overlap. 感じる かんじる emphasizes feeling or sensing. There is no general lexical antonym; 思わない means "do not think".

## Distinctive meaning

と思います presents a view rather than an established fact. It does not necessarily mean uncertainty, and 思う is not restricted to emotions. The negative sentence この本は高くないと思います このほんはたかくないとおもいます means "I think this book isn't expensive": the negative belongs inside the thought.

# 考える (かんがえる) — think about; consider

## Meaning

考える means thinking about something, considering it, or working out an idea. It can also express a considered judgment or plan.

- この問題を考えてください。 (このもんだいをかんがえてください。) — Please think about this problem.
- 何を食べるか考えています。 (なにをたべるかかんがえています。) — I am thinking about what to eat.

In the second example, 何を食べるか, "what to eat," is the question being considered.

## How the kanji combine

This is one native verb: [考](../kanji/考.md) supplies かんが, and える is okurigana.
It is ichidan: 考えます (かんがえます), 考えて (かんがえて), 考えた (かんがえた), 考えない (かんがえない).
The related noun 考え (かんがえ) can mean a thought, idea, or opinion.

## Synonyms and antonyms

- [思う](思う.md) (おもう) often expresses an opinion, impression, or feeling. 考える more readily emphasizes thinking something through.
- 悩む (なやむ) means being troubled or worried; thinking about a choice does not necessarily mean worrying about it.
- There is no single general antonym. 考えない (かんがえない) simply means not thinking about or considering something.

## Distinctive meaning

The contrast with 思う is a tendency, not a logical/emotional split. Both can express judgments.
For a problem you are actively working through, 考える is useful; for an immediate "I think..." opinion,
思う is often natural. Choose the whole expression rather than treating English "think" as a one-word translation rule.

Use **matter を判断する** for what you assess, or **conclusion と判断する** for the conclusion reached.

- これは危険だと判断しました。 (これはきけんだとはんだんしました。) — I judged that this was dangerous.
- 自分で判断してください。 (じぶんではんだんしてください。) — Please judge for yourself.

In the first sentence, 危険だ is the conclusion and と introduces it.
The だ belongs to the plain predicate 危険だ, "is dangerous."

## How the kanji combine

[判](../kanji/判.md) contributes judging, and [断](../kanji/断.md) has a decision or judgment sense here.
The two reinforce reaching a judgment; 断 is not describing physically cutting an object in this word.
The on readings are ハン + ダン.

## Synonyms and antonyms

決断 けつだん means a decision or determination, useful when the focus is committing to a course of action.
判断 can instead report an assessment, such as judging that something is dangerous, without stating what action follows.
The meanings overlap, so this is a practical contrast rather than a ban on translating either as "decision."

## Distinctive meaning

判断 does not guarantee that the conclusion is correct.
It identifies the act or result of judging; the evidence and the person making the judgment still matter.
In the danger example, we learn the speaker's assessment, not automatically a final plan or an established fact.

# 検査 (けんさ) - inspection; examination

## Meaning

検査 is an inspection, examination, or test that checks a condition or detects a problem. **Nを検査する** means to inspect or test N. **検査を受ける** (けんさをうける) means to undergo a test or examination.

- 工場で製品を検査します。 (こうじょうでせいひんをけんさします。) - We inspect the products at the factory.
- 明日、病院で検査を受けます。 (あした、びょういんでけんさをうけます。) - I am having a medical test at the hospital tomorrow.

The first subject performs the inspection; the second person receives it. 検査の結果 (けんさのけっか) is "the test results."

## How the kanji combine

検 contributes checking or examining, and [査](../kanji/査.md) contributes investigating or examining. The near-synonymous components reinforce careful checking. Their on readings are ケン + サ.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[試験](試験.md) (しけん) includes examinations of knowledge and tests of performance. [調査](調査.md) (ちょうさ) concerns investigation or gathering information. [検討](検討.md) (けんとう) is considering or examining a proposal, rather than automatically testing a physical item.

## Distinctive meaning

検査 can apply to medical samples, factory products, and baggage. It does not by itself mean that a problem was found or that treatment was given. Use the context to decide between English "inspection," "test," "scan," and "examination."

# 調査 (ちょうさ) - investigation; survey

## Meaning

調査 is an investigation, inquiry, or survey carried out to obtain information.
調査する is transitive: 原因を調査する (げんいんをちょうさする), "investigate the cause."
As a noun, Xについての調査 is "an investigation/survey about X."

- 警察が事故の原因を調査しています。 (けいさつがじこのげんいんをちょうさしています。) - The police are investigating the cause of the accident.
- 学生の生活について調査を行いました。 (がくせいのせいかつについてちょうさをおこないました。) - We conducted a survey of students' lives.

調査の結果 (ちょうさのけっか) means "the results of the investigation/survey."
調査中 (ちょうさちゅう) means "under investigation" or "a survey is in progress."

## How the kanji combine

[調](../kanji/調.md) contributes examining or checking in this word, and [査](../kanji/査.md) inspection.
Their combined meaning centers on finding out facts.
The on-readings are チョウ + サ.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[調べる](調べる.md) (しらべる) is a broader everyday verb for looking into or checking something.
[研究](研究.md) (けんきゅう) is research; collecting survey information may be part of a larger research project.
[質問](質問.md) (しつもん) is a question or questioning, one possible method rather than the whole investigation.

## Distinctive meaning

調査 does not specify a questionnaire. Investigators might inspect a site, read records, interview people,
or combine methods.
Nor does 調査中 imply that the answer is already known: it identifies an ongoing inquiry rather than its conclusion.

# 比較 (ひかく) - comparison

## Meaning

比較 is comparison. 比較する is a transitive する verb: **A と B を比較する**, "compare A and B," or **A を B と比較する**, "compare A with B."

- 二つの製品の値段を比較しました。 (ふたつのせいひんのねだんをひかくしました。) - I compared the prices of the two products.
- 去年と比較すると、今年は雨が少ないです。 (きょねんとひかくすると、ことしはあめがすくないです。) - Compared with last year, there is less rain this year.

The second example uses と比較すると to establish the reference for a judgment. A noun phrase such as 二つの案の比較 (ふたつのあんのひかく) means "a comparison of two proposals."

## How the kanji combine

[比](../kanji/比.md) contributes comparing or setting things side by side; 較 also contributes comparison. The two reinforce the same central action. The on readings are ヒ + カク.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[比べる](比べる.md) (くらべる) is the corresponding everyday verb "compare." [判断](判断.md) (はんだん) is judgment or assessment, which may follow a comparison but is not the comparison itself.

## Distinctive meaning

比較 does not automatically mean deciding a winner. A comparison can describe similarities, differences, prices, or changes over time. State the dimension when useful, as with 値段を比較する. Also distinguish 比較 from 比較的 (ひかくてき), "relatively," which is a related adverbial expression rather than the noun alone.

# 比べる (くらべる) - to compare

## Meaning

比べる means to compare two or more things. A useful pattern is AとBを比べる, "compare A and B." AをBと比べる presents B as the comparison partner.

- 二つの店の値段を比べました。 (ふたつのみせのねだんをくらべました。) - I compared the prices at the two shops.
- 去年と比べて、今年は暖かいです。 (きょねんとくらべて、ことしはあたたかいです。) - Compared with last year, this year is warm.

It is a transitive ichidan verb: 比べます, 比べない, 比べて. Both と比べて and に比べて can introduce a standard of comparison.

## How the kanji combine

[比](../kanji/比.md) expresses comparison; べる is the written okurigana. The grammatical stem used before ます is くらべ, not just the portion represented by the kanji.

## Synonyms and antonyms

比較する (ひかくする) is a more formal equivalent. 選ぶ (えらぶ), "choose," describes a possible next step after comparing, not the comparison itself.

## Distinctive meaning

比べる does not imply deciding which item is better. You can compare sizes, prices, or similarities without selecting a winner. The comparison must be supplied by the context or named explicitly.

# 計算 (けいさん) - calculation

## Meaning

計算 is a calculation or the process of working something out numerically.
計算する is transitive: 費用を計算する (ひようをけいさんする), "calculate the cost."
The noun can also concern estimation or taking something into account.

- 旅行に必要な費用を計算しました。 (りょこうにひつようなひようをけいさんしました。) - I calculated the expenses needed for the trip.
- 電卓を使わずに計算してください。 (でんたくをつかわずにけいさんしてください。) - Please do the calculation without using a calculator.

The second sentence leaves the numbers understood from context; it does not change the verb into a different action.

## How the kanji combine

[計](../kanji/計.md) contributes counting or measuring, and [算](../kanji/算.md) calculation.
Their meanings reinforce each other in the on-reading compound ケイ + サン.
The result names the calculation, not the device used to perform it.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[数える](数える.md) (かぞえる) focuses on counting items.
計算 can involve addition, division, or other operations beyond counting one by one.
[予算](予算.md) (よさん) is a budget: calculation may be needed to prepare it, but it is not the same noun.

## Distinctive meaning

計算に入れる (けいさんにいれる), "take into account," can extend beyond arithmetic:
遅れる可能性も計算に入れる (おくれるかのうせいもけいさんにいれる), "allow for the possibility of delay too."
This use concerns planning or estimation, not necessarily entering a number into a calculator.

# 胸 (むね) - chest; breast; feelings

## Meaning

胸 is a noun for the chest or breast area. It also appears in expressions about one's heart, thoughts, or feelings. The same word can therefore describe a physical location or an emotional experience.

- 胸に手を当てました。 (むねにてをあてました。) - I put my hand on my chest.
- うれしくて胸がいっぱいになりました。 (うれしくてむねがいっぱいになりました。) - I was overwhelmed with happiness.

The second sentence describes being filled with emotion, not a physical object filling the chest.

## How the kanji combine

[胸](../kanji/胸.md) is one character with the native reading むね. The dictionary also records むな, used especially in compounds. Learn the reading of a compound separately rather than changing むね to むな in an ordinary standalone sentence.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[腹](腹.md) (はら) refers to the belly, a neighboring but different body area. [心](心.md) (こころ), "heart/mind," overlaps with emotional uses, but it is not a replacement for the physical chest in the first example.

## Distinctive meaning

胸 can refer to someone's breasts in a suitable context, but it is not restricted to that meaning or to one gender. 胸が痛い (むねがいたい) can concern physical chest pain or emotional distress; surrounding information determines the meaning. Do not convert every figurative 胸 expression into an anatomical claim.

# 知る (しる) — know; find out

## Meaning

知る means knowing something or coming to know it. A useful first distinction is between 知りました (しりました),
"found out," and 知っています (しっています), "know."

- その人を知っています。 (そのひとをしっています。) — I know that person.
- きのう、そのことを知りました。 (きのう、そのことをしりました。) — I found out about that yesterday.

For "I don't know," the ordinary polite form is 知りません (しりません). The positive and negative do not
normally use matching ている forms in this basic exchange.

## How the kanji combine

This is a single native verb. [知](../kanji/知.md) supplies し; る is okurigana.
Despite the i-sound before る, it is a godan verb: 知ります (しります), 知って (しって), 知らない (しらない).

## Synonyms and antonyms

- [分かる](分かる.md) (わかる) often emphasizes understanding. 知っている can mean that you know a fact without fully understanding it.
- [習う](習う.md) (ならう) means learning under instruction, not simply finding out a piece of news.
- 忘れる (わすれる), "forget," means losing access to something you knew. Merely not knowing is 知らない (しらない), not necessarily forgetting.

## Distinctive meaning

知っている is useful for familiarity with people, places, and facts. The thing known normally takes を.
Do not turn the contrast with 分かる into a rigid rule: dictionary senses overlap, and the natural verb depends
on what kind of knowing or understanding the sentence describes.

# 覚える (おぼえる) — memorize; remember

## Meaning

覚える means to memorize, learn by heart, or remember. The item learned takes を.
It is an ichidan verb: 覚えます (おぼえます), 覚えた (おぼえた).

- 新しい言葉を十個覚えました。 (あたらしいことばをじゅっこおぼえました。) — I learned ten new words.
- その名前を覚えています。 (そのなまえをおぼえています。) — I remember that name.

The second example describes retaining something in memory, not necessarily studying it right now.

## How the kanji combine

[覚](../kanji/覚.md) supplies the memory association in this native verb. The える after it
completes おぼえる and changes with the ending. Do not replace it with the ending of 覚める
(さめる), "wake up": that is a different word.

## Synonyms and antonyms

思い出す (おもいだす) focuses on recalling something from memory.
覚える can instead describe putting it into memory, as in learning the new words above.
[忘れる](../words/忘れる.md) (わすれる), "forget," is a useful contrast to retaining it.

## Distinctive meaning

English "remember" covers both keeping something in mind and bringing it back to mind.
Compare 名前を覚えている (なまえをおぼえている), "remember a name,"
with 名前を思い出す (なまえをおもいだす), "recall a name."
This article focuses on the memory sense, not every use of 覚える.

# 予想 (よそう) — prediction; expectation

## Meaning

予想 is an expectation or prediction about what will happen. It is also used with する as a verb.
For a predicted statement, put a plain-form clause before と予想する.

- 明日は雨が降ると予想しています。 (あしたはあめがふるとよそうしています。) — I expect it to rain tomorrow.
- 試合の結果を予想しました。 (しあいのけっかをよそうしました。) — I predicted the result of the match.

The first predicts a statement; the second uses を for the outcome being predicted.

## How the kanji combine

[予](../kanji/予.md) contributes "beforehand"; [想](../kanji/想.md) concerns a thought or conception.
Together they suggest thinking ahead to an outcome. The on readings are ヨ + ソウ.
The combination names a prediction, not a promise that it will come true.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[予定](予定.md) (よてい) concerns plans or arrangements, though its dictionary meanings also include
expectation and estimate. A useful contrast is predicting rain versus scheduling a meeting.
想像 (そうぞう), "imagination," need not be about a future event.

## Distinctive meaning

A 予想 can be wrong. It does not establish that the speaker controls the event or has arranged it.
Use the whole construction 雨が降ると予想する (あめがふるとよそうする);
と links the predicted statement to the prediction verb.

# 会計 (かいけい) - accounting; bill

## Meaning

会計 is a noun for accounting or managing financial accounts. Depending on context, it can also mean the person handling the money, a restaurant bill, or settling that bill with 会計する.

- クラブの会計を担当しています。 (クラブのかいけいをたんとうしています。) - I am responsible for the club's accounts.
- お会計をお願いします。 (おかいけいをおねがいします。) - The bill, please.

# 支払う (しはらう) — pay

## Meaning

支払う means to pay. The bill, fee, or amount paid takes を; the means of payment can take で.
It is a verb, not a noun requiring する.

- 料金をカードで支払います。 (りょうきんをカードでしはらいます。) — I will pay the fee by card.
- 家賃はもう支払いました。 (やちんはもうしはらいました。) — I have already paid the rent.

The past form is 支払った (しはらった); the negative is 支払わない (しはらわない).

## How the kanji combine

JMdict explicitly identifies [支](../kanji/支.md) as **ateji** here: a character used for its sound,
not a reliable literal contribution such as "support."
[払](../kanji/払.md) corresponds to はらう, "pay." Do not explain the word as "support + pay."

The spelling mixes し with the native reading はらう. Under this repository's on-first mixed-reading convention
it is filed as `kango`; that is a display classification, not a claim that this is an ordinary two-on-reading compound
or proof of its historical derivation.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[払う](払う.md) (はらう) also means "pay": 料金を払う (りょうきんをはらう) is another way to say "pay the fee."
But 払う also has nonfinancial uses, such as ほこりを払う, "brush off the dust."
支払う is not a replacement for 払う in that dusting expression.

## Distinctive meaning

Learn 支払う as a payment verb with its own spelling. Its extra character does not make it a combination
of providing support and making a payment. もう支払いました (もうしはらいました), "I have already paid,"
reports that the payment was made; it is not a general expression for handing any object to somebody.

# 誤解 (ごかい) — misunderstanding

## Meaning

誤解 is a misunderstanding: someone interprets something incorrectly.
It can be a noun or combine with する.

- 私の言葉を誤解しないでください。 (わたしのことばをごかいしないでください。) — Please do not misunderstand what I said.
- それは誤解です。 (それはごかいです。) — That is a misunderstanding.

In the first example, を marks the words being misunderstood.

## How the kanji combine

[誤](../kanji/誤.md), "mistaken," qualifies [解](../kanji/解.md), "understanding."
The error is in the interpretation. The on readings are ゴ + カイ, giving ごかい.
This is not simply a synonym for every kind of mistake.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[理解](../words/理解.md) (りかい) is understanding or comprehension. It gives the useful contrast,
but not understanding at all and misunderstanding are different situations:
誤解 suggests that the interpretation is wrong, rather than merely absent.

## Distinctive meaning

誤解 does not necessarily imply deliberate deception. It can arise even when nobody intended
to mislead anyone. A useful phrase is 誤解を解く (ごかいをとく), "clear up a misunderstanding":
解く here means resolving or dispelling it, not physically undoing an object.

# 間違い (まちがい) - mistake; error

## Meaning

間違い is a noun meaning "mistake" or "error." Use 間違いがある
for containing a mistake, and 間違いを直す for correcting one.
間違いです identifies something as wrong.

- 名前に間違いがないか、確認してください。 (なまえにまちがいがないか、かくにんしてください。) - Please check whether the name is correct.

The second example literally asks whether there is no mistake in
the name. 間違いない can also express certainty: "there is
no doubt" or "it is definitely so."

[間](../kanji/間.md) contributes an interval or relation, and
[違](../kanji/違.md) contributes difference or deviation.
間違い is the noun associated with 間違う (まちがう).
The established word means an error; "wrong interval" is not a
literal definition or a verified historical explanation.

[誤り](誤り.md) (あやまり) also names an error.
[間違える](間違える.md) (まちがえる) is a verb for making
a mistake or confusing things. [正しい](正しい.md)
(ただしい), "correct," supplies a contrasting evaluation but is
an adjective, not a noun synonym.

The noun does not identify the cause or seriousness of an error.

# 誤り (あやまり) - error; mistake

## Meaning

誤り is a noun for an error or mistake, including an incorrect statement, calculation, or judgment.
Use 誤りがある for "contain an error" and 誤りを直す (あやまりをなおす) for "correct an error."

- この計算には誤りがあります。 (このけいさんにはあやまりがあります。) - There is an error in this calculation.
- 名前の誤りを直してください。 (なまえのあやまりをなおしてください。) - Please correct the mistake in the name.

The thing containing the error can take に, while の identifies the area in which it occurs.
誤りを認める (あやまりをみとめる) means "acknowledge a mistake."

## How the kanji combine

[誤](../kanji/誤.md) conveys being mistaken. 誤り is the noun related to 誤る (あやまる), "make a mistake";
the written り belongs to the native word. It is not read with the on reading ご found in [誤解](誤解.md).

## Synonyms and antonyms

[間違い](間違い.md) (まちがい) overlaps broadly with "mistake."
誤解 (ごかい) specifically concerns a mistaken interpretation, whereas a typing or arithmetic error need not involve misunderstanding.
[正しい](正しい.md) (ただしい), "correct," provides a contrast in judgment, not a noun that can replace 誤り grammatically.

## Distinctive meaning

Calling something an 誤り identifies it as incorrect, without saying whether it was deliberate.
Do not confuse あやまり with 謝り, the noun related to [謝る](謝る.md) (あやまる), "apologize":
admitting an error and offering an apology are different actions.

# ミス (ミス) - mistake; Miss

## Meaning

ミス is a mistake, error, or blunder. It is a noun and can take する:
ミスをする or ミスする means making a mistake. A separate same-spelling word
is the title "Miss" or "Ms.," used as a prefix.

- 計算でミスをしました。 (けいさんでミスをしました。) - I made a mistake in the calculation.
- 同じミスを繰り返さないようにします。 (おなじミスをくりかえさないようにします。) - I will try not to repeat the same mistake.

For the separate title, ミス・スミス means "Miss Smith." This is not a description
of an error made by Smith.

## How the kanji combine

These words are written in katakana. The mistake entry records English "miss"
as its source; do not assume that ミス is simply a Japanese shortening of the
whole English word "mistake." The personal-title use belongs to a separate
dictionary identity.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[間違い](間違い.md) (まちがい) also means a mistake.
[失敗](失敗.md) (しっぱい) concerns failure or an unsuccessful attempt. A small
ミス can be corrected without the entire project becoming a failure.

## Distinctive meaning

The error sense does not automatically imply dishonesty or intentional
rule-breaking. Keep it distinct from [不正](不正.md) (ふせい).
The title sense is not a general replacement for さん in everyday Japanese
address; it belongs to contexts using that title. Neither identity means
"miss someone" in the emotional English sense.

# 失敗 (しっぱい) — failure; mistake

## Meaning

失敗 is a failure, mistake, or blunder. Add する to describe an attempt going wrong: 失敗する (しっぱいする).
An activity or undertaking can be marked with に, as in 料理に失敗する, "make an unsuccessful attempt at cooking."

- 料理に失敗しました。 (りょうりにしっぱいしました。) — My attempt at cooking went wrong.
- 一度失敗しても、またやってみます。 (いちどしっぱいしても、またやってみます。) — Even if I fail once, I will try again.

## How the kanji combine

[失](../kanji/失.md) brings the idea of loss or error; [敗](../kanji/敗.md) brings failure or defeat.
The meanings reinforce an unsuccessful result rather than forming a literal object-and-action phrase.
シツ + ハイ becomes しっぱい: the small っ and the following ぱ are part of the word's pronunciation.

## Synonyms and antonyms

成功 (せいこう), "success," gives a direct contrast for an undertaking: 成功する versus 失敗する.
間違い (まちがい) means a mistake or error, such as an incorrect answer or calculation.
The words overlap, but an incorrect detail and the failure of an entire attempt are not necessarily the same event.

## Distinctive meaning

失敗 evaluates what happened against an intended result. It need not mean that a person is generally incapable.
For losing an object rather than failing at an attempt, 失う (うしなう), "lose," is a different verb despite the shared character.
Learn the construction with the situation, not just an English label such as "fail."

# 定規 (じょうぎ) — ruler

## Meaning

定規 is a ruler. It names the physical tool, as in drawing a straight line, rather than a rule
that tells people how to behave.

- 定規でまっすぐな線を引きます。 (じょうぎでまっすぐなせんをひきます。) — I draw a straight line with a ruler.
- 定規を貸してください。 (じょうぎをかしてください。) — Please lend me a ruler.

In the first sentence, で marks the tool used.

## How the kanji combine

[定](../kanji/定.md) contributes the idea of something fixed or established,
and [規](../kanji/規.md) that of a measure or standard. Together they name a tool that
provides a fixed guide. The on-reading compound is じょうぎ: the 規 reading キ is voiced to ギ.

## Synonyms and antonyms

物差し (ものさし) also means a ruler or measuring stick. It overlaps with 定規 as the name
of a tool; its dictionary senses also include a figurative standard or yardstick.
That does not make every use of the two words interchangeable.

## Distinctive meaning

The character 規 appears in words about rules, but the selected meaning of 定規 is concrete.
In the examples, you can use it or lend it. Keep the complete reading じょうぎ together
rather than guessing a reading from one character at a time.

# 違い (ちがい) - difference; discrepancy

## Meaning

違い is a noun for a difference or distinction. AとBの違い means "the difference between A and B."
Use 違いがある for "there is a difference" and 違いが分かる for "understand or notice the difference."

- この二つの言葉の違いが分かりますか。 (このふたつのことばのちがいがわかりますか。) - Do you understand the difference between these two words?
- 値段には大きな違いがあります。 (ねだんにはおおきなちがいがあります。) - There is a large difference in price.

An adjective can modify the noun: 大きな違い is a large difference, and 小さな違い
(ちいさなちがい) is a small one.

## How the kanji combine

[違](../kanji/違.md) supplies the idea of differing or diverging.
違い is related to the verb [違う](違う.md) (ちがう), "differ; be different."
The final い is part of a noun form here, not an i-adjective ending:
use 違いがある rather than conjugating it like 高い.

## Synonyms and antonyms

[共通](共通.md) (きょうつう), "shared; in common," gives the contrasting viewpoint.
[間違い](間違い.md) (まちがい) usually identifies a mistake. A 違い can be neutral:
two colors or prices need not involve anyone making an error.

## Distinctive meaning

The noun identifies a distinction without necessarily judging one side correct or superior.
When comparing language forms, specify which aspect differs: meaning, usage, pronunciation, or politeness.
AとBの違い names the comparison itself; the sentence still needs to explain what the difference is.

# 違う (ちがう) — be different

## Meaning

違う means being different. Use AはBと違う to compare A with B; と marks the comparison point.
Although English uses the adjective "different," Japanese 違う is a verb.

- 私の答えはあなたの答えと違います。 (わたしのこたえはあなたのこたえとちがいます。) — My answer is different from yours.
- この二つは色が違います。 (このふたつはいろがちがいます。) — These two are different colors.

## How the kanji combine

[違](../kanji/違.md) carries the difference meaning, and う completes the native verb ちがう.
The polite form is 違います (ちがいます), not 違いです. Before a noun, 違う色 (ちがういろ) means "a different color."

## Synonyms and antonyms

間違う (まちがう) concerns being mistaken or making a mistake.
違う can also mean "be incorrect," but a neutral comparison of two colors need not identify an error.
The noun 違い (ちがい) means "difference."

## Distinctive meaning

A reply such as 違います (ちがいます) may correct a statement: "That is not right."
This corrective use and the neutral "differ" use belong to the same verb; the surrounding conversation supplies the intended judgment.

Dictionary: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entries 1158870, 1158880, 1611610.
